text:
sarah: :rotating_light: noticing ~12 GPU nodes in us-east1-b went NotReady and got a NoSchedule taint this morning, started ~07:12 UTC. pods with nodeSelector=gpu are PENDING.

mike: looking now, getting reports from cluster-autoscaler that nodes are being considered unready and scale-down is blocked. can you paste the kubelet logs for one node?

sarah: here is the kubelet syslog excerpt from node gpu-us-east1b-07:

```
Jul 14 07:13:02 gpu-us-east1b-07 kubelet[1234]: device plugin: failed to start: nvidia-device-plugin v0.11.0: plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = could not init controller: nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: cannot set namespace for GPU device: operation not permitted
Jul 14 07:13:02 gpu-us-east1b-07 kubelet[1234]: kubelet: node status set to NotReady
```

leo: that nvidia-container-cli error rings a bell — we recently rolled the driver to 535.60 on the pool. possible seccomp or cgroup v2 interaction on that node image? are these nodes on the new cos_containerd image?

sarah: yes these are the new cos-containerd pool we created last week. older pool (cos) unaffected.

anna: I see the device-plugin ds logs show repeated failures to allocate and then crashloop: `Failed to allocate: running 'nvidia-container-cli' failed: unknown error: container runtime error: init failed: cannot set ns`

mike: cluster-autoscaler snapshot: it marked 10 nodes as Unready and didn't scale up because pending pods request 8 GPUs each and the autoscaler only sees partial capacity. we risk downstream training jobs timing out.

sarah: quick mitigation — cordon the remaining new pool nodes so CA won't pick them, and spin up a temporary dedicated pool using the previous base image (cos) with driver 525 to restore capacity. I can cordon the bad nodes.

leo: +1 on fallback pool. long term we need to pin driver+node-image matrix. also we should revert the daemonset image to v0.10 which had a different UID mapping workaround.

mike: trying a quick test on one node: patched nvidia-device-plugin to run privileged and mount /run/docker.sock to see if it's a permission issue. results: plugin started but we see warnings about seccomp profile denied syscalls.

sarah: can you share the exact kubectl patch?

mike: `kubectl -n kube-system patch ds nvidia-device-plugin --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/privileged","value":true}]'`

anna: that unblocks allocation but running workloads fail later with `nvidia-container-cli: failed to set cgroup attributes: permission denied`. so two different permission surfaces.

leo: looks like cos-containerd + driver 535 + containerd seccomp defaults = broken on our current device-plugin version. we saw a similar but not identical issue in EU region last year, but that was kernel module mismatch. this one is userns or seccomp-related.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - gpu nodes NotReady in us-east1-b (assigned: mike).

mike: plan: 1) cordon and drain non-critical workloads from the bad pool. 2) create a temporary pool on cos with driver 525 + device-plugin v0.10, attach to nodepools so CA can scale it. 3) prepare a canary: update 1 node in new pool with a patched device-plugin image that sets --disable-nvidia-ctr-checks and runs privileged to validate. 4) if canary passes, roll patch; otherwise rollback driver to 525 across pool.

sarah: doing step 1 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-us-east1b-* && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` on the more flaky nodes.

anna: I'm starting the temp pool with terraform module `redwood-gpu-pool` and pinning image to cos and driver to 525. should be up in ~9m.

mike: I pushed a patched device-plugin image to our internal registry: `registry.redwood/inference/nvidia-device-plugin:canary-priv`. I'm going to patch the daemonset on one node via nodeSelector for canary.

leo: when you run the canary, please capture `dmesg`, kubelet logs, and `journalctl -u nvidia-driver-install.service` if present. also check `lsmod | grep nvidia` to confirm kernel module versions.

sarah: temp pool ready, CA is scheduling backlogged jobs there. training queue is moving again. :relieved:

mike: canary started, allocation succeeded for a simple gpu-sample pod. running a multi-GPU job now to stress.

anna: cost note — creating temp pool on cos (non-preemptible) will add ~$2k/day if kept longer than necessary. recommend we keep it only until root cause is fixed or rollback applied.

leo: initial canary stress run failed with `nvidia-container-cli: failed to set ns` after ~3m under load. sending logs to /inc.

mike: given canary failed, schedule is rollback driver to 525 on the cos-containerd pool nodes. coordinate maintenance window 11:00 UTC for rolling driver downgrade to avoid further impact.

sarah: I've uncordoned the healthy older pool and moved remaining critical jobs there. I'll keep the temp pool until downgrade completes.

anna: I'll notify platform consumers in #ml-infra and ask teams to postpone heavy runs until after 12:30 UTC.

mike: owners: mike (driver rollback), anna (temp pool + comms), sarah (node remediation + CA watches), leo (postmortem writeup). I'll open a PR to pin the allowed node-image/driver combinations in our node pool provisioning docs and enforce in terraform.

sarah: thanks team. filing follow-ups: add e2e tests for cos-containerd+driver-535 matrix, update docs, and add an alert for device-plugin crashloops that triggers earlier. :white_check_mark:
